ai.description: *Limnonectes ghoshi* is a small frog (SVL ~30–40 mm) with a brown dorsum and pale venter. It features a distinct dark interorbital bar and a robust, broad head with prominent vomerine teeth.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Limnonectes ghoshi* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, dark-colored supratympanic fold that extends from behind the eye to the shoulder.
ai.habitat: *Limnonectes ghoshi* inhabits the humid, dense evergreen forests of Northeast India, typically found near rocky streams at elevations between 1,000 and 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Manipur frog is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for small invertebrates near forest streams and damp, rocky habitats.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Limnonectes ghoshi* is an oviparous frog that breeds during the monsoon season (June–August), laying small clutches of eggs in rocky, stream-side microhabitats.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Limnonectes ghoshi* is endemic to the Indian state of Manipur, specifically inhabiting high-elevation forest streams in the Northeast region.
ai.callDescription: The *Limnonectes ghoshi* emits a series of high-pitched, rhythmic "tink-tink" notes, typically heard while the frog is perched near fast-flowing streams in forested habitats.
